answer: Each agent can post one claim per epoch only after locking a scarce, slashable bond, while independent peers challenge claims with signed evidence. A random audit samples claims; if two identities trace to the same controller or fabricated work, the bond is slashed and challengers share the penalty. Splitting into sybils therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must immobilize more capital and risks losing it. A raven watching the wharf can flag a suspicious thread, but evidence, not names, triggers enforcement.
